strings.name: João Lourenço
strings.role: President of Angola and leader of the MPLA
strings.summary: João Lourenço has been president of Angola since 2017 and leader of the governing People's Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) since 2018. He advocates anti-corruption measures and economic reform, has participated in regional peace diplomacy, and held the rotating African Union chairmanship in 2025–2026. Electoral disputes and human rights concerns also shape assessments of his presidency.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026, including an interview report published on 14 November. The AU chairmanship changed hands in February 2026. Candidacy for party leader is distinguished from the party's candidate in the 2027 national election.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Angola's economic adjustment and has participated in mediation between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, influencing African security cooperation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and background
strings.facts.f1.value: Born on 5 March 1954 in Lobito, Benguela province, Angola. His full name is João Manuel Gonçalves Lourenço. His political career spans the military, provincial administration, parliament and cabinet.
strings.facts.f2.label: Parliamentary and administrative experience
strings.facts.f2.value: Appointed provincial commissioner of Moxico in 1983 and of Benguela from 1986 to 1989. He was first vice-president of the National Assembly from 2003 to 2014, before becoming defence minister.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Anti-corruption pledges and party leadership
strings.highlights.h1.text: On taking over the governing party in 2018, he pledged to combat corruption, nepotism and impunity, including within the party. These commitments and personnel changes do not by themselves demonstrate that corruption was eliminated or economic diversification completed.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Electoral and civil-rights disputes
strings.highlights.h2.text: A 2022 UN report records opposition challenges to the election result and the court's decision to uphold it. Human Rights Watch's World Report 2026 criticises protest policing, arbitrary detention and restrictions on press freedom during 2025. These criticisms are not a judicial finding of personal criminal liability against Lourenço.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Explains party and national election arrangements
strings.timeline.t1.text: DW and Lusa reported his comments on succession at the opening of an industrial technology centre in Luanda. Central Committee approval on 5 November of his candidacy for party leader did not constitute re-election. He said the party's candidate for the 2027 national election had yet to be announced.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Hands over the rotating AU chairmanship
strings.timeline.t2.text: At the Addis Ababa summit, Burundi's President Évariste Ndayishimiye succeeded him as rotating AU chair. This office, held by a head of state or government, is distinct from chairperson of the African Union Commission.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes rotating AU chair
strings.timeline.t3.text: Took over the one-year chairmanship at the opening of the 38th AU summit. In April that year he supported Togolese leader Faure Gnassingbé's succession to his DRC–Rwanda mediation role. The transfer of responsibility did not mean the conflict had been resolved.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Begins a second presidential term
strings.timeline.t4.text: Following the 24 August election, the electoral commission reported 51.17% of votes for the MPLA. The opposition challenged the result, which the Constitutional Court declared final on 8 September. He was sworn in on 15 September; polling, adjudication and inauguration are separate dates.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Elected MPLA leader
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded José Eduardo dos Santos at a party congress, adding leadership of the governing party to the presidency. The party handover occurred almost a year after the presidential transition, not on the same day.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First inauguration as president of Angola
strings.timeline.t6.text: Succeeded dos Santos after the MPLA won the 23 August general election. Under the constitution, the person heading the national list of the party or coalition receiving the most votes becomes president; there is no separate presidential ballot.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes defence minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: Appointed defence minister by presidential decree, serving until the start of the 2017 election campaign. His earlier service as first vice-president of parliament is recorded separately from this ministerial term.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Undertakes military education in the Soviet Union
strings.timeline.t8.text: Received military training in the Soviet Union from 1978 to 1982, specialising in heavy artillery. Angola's foreign ministry biography also records a master's degree in historical sciences there, without establishing its precise institution or award date.
